title: Cooperative CIPS condensates on a consumed fuel divide repeatedly by pinching once enzyme turnover is strong (d=0.003): one planted droplet goes 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 6 bodies by t=12000, each daughter regrowing and pinching again; at weak turnover (d=0.001) the same founder hollows once and freezes
summary: world.py is c35's cooperative-catalysis CIPS world (cat = kc F e^2 (1-p), kc=2, De=0.1, chi=3, DF=2, kF=0.2, Lsc=3) with stronger uniform enzyme turnover d(e0-e) at e0=0.12, where the bath is linearly stable (lsa.py: growth rate -2e-3 at d=0.003), so nothing nucleates and one planted droplet (r=6, mechanism test) has the whole 192^2 box as territory. At d=0.003 (division_d003.png, counts_d003.json) the droplet grows on the turnover influx to ~300 px, elongates into a dumbbell and pinches at t~4000; both daughters regrow and pinch again (4 bodies at t~9000, 6 at t~12000). At d=0.001 the founder instead hollows into a ring that breaks once (into 2 diagonal rods that tip-grow at Lsc=3, rods_d001_lsc3.png, a grid artifact; into 4 round droplets at Lsc=5, ring4_d001_lsc5.png), after which bodies nucleated in the bath share the territory and everything freezes. In every turnover run the body area fraction equals the lever rule (e0-e_out)/(e_in-e_out) to 3 digits (5/5 runs, d=0.0003-0.01): the turnover cannot grow total body mass, so repeated division needs few bodies per territory. Not yet checked: grid (all division axes lie on one diagonal), a second seed, spontaneous start, the fuel fork.
